subject: chemistry
title: The ideal gas equation
key_idea: Gas pressure comes from particles colliding with the container wall. An ideal gas has particles of zero volume with no forces between them. Its pressure, volume, amount and temperature are linked by pV = nRT, with every quantity in SI units.

blocks.text: Gas particles move randomly at high speed. This section covers how that motion produces pressure.

items: Particles collide with the walls of the container.
Each collision exerts a tiny force on the wall.
Pressure is the total force of these collisions per unit area of wall.
More frequent or harder collisions mean higher pressure, for example at higher temperature or in a smaller volume.
Pressure comes from particles hitting the container wall.
Pressure is force per unit area.

blocks.text: An ideal gas is a model that makes the equation exact. Real gases behave almost ideally at high temperature and low pressure.

items.meaning: A gas whose particles have zero volume and no intermolecular forces of attraction.

items: The particles are treated as points, with no volume of their own.
There are no forces of attraction between the particles.
Collisions with the walls are perfectly elastic: no kinetic energy is lost.
Real gases deviate when particles are close together (high pressure) or slow (low temperature), because the particles then have volume and attract each other.
Ideal gas: zero particle volume, no intermolecular forces.
Real gases act most ideally at high temperature and low pressure.

checks.q: Explain how a gas exerts pressure on the walls of its container.
checks.a: Gas particles move randomly and collide with the walls. Each collision exerts a force, and the force of many collisions per unit area is the pressure.
